Subject: Post-call: FastRetail discovery + Redwood vs hyperscalers cost/TCO

Hi Annie / Ethan —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the action items we agreed on:  

- Goals: move from prototype to production for personalized recommendations in checkout (latency goal p95 < 120ms) and conversational search across product catalog.
- Traffic profile: ~5k reqs/sec peak with highly spiky seasonal bursts; average request uses ~1.2k tokens (prompt + expected response).
- Data controls: customer data must remain in FastRetail VPC for PII-sensitive flows; SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration required.

Key differentiation points we discussed vs hyperscalers:  
- Equivalent quality to managed APIs with 20–40% lower per-token unit cost for steady-state inference due to batching + kernel optimizations.
- Predictable reserved capacity (Dedicated) to avoid throttling during peak with contract-backed SLOs.
- Transparent tooling for token-level cost, cache hit metrics, and rollback/rollout controls.

Open items / next steps:  
1) I’ll share a short one-pager comparing Redwood to AWS Bedrock / GCP Vertex AI performance and an initial TCO model for per-1M tokens (attached).
2) Aditya (SE) will propose the concrete test plan: latency/throughput runs, cache-hit simulation, and quantization matrix.
3) Monica (CS) will surface SOC 2 artifact timeline and KMS options.
4) Annie/Ethan: please confirm the procurement contact and any contract constraints (term, IP clauses).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-one-pager.pdf, tco_modeling_1M_tokens.xlsx, demo-recording-20260313.mp4

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up next week if you'd like to walk the numbers together.

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-call: FastRetail discovery + Redwood vs hyperscalers cost/TCO

Great questions — answering at a high level here, Aditya will follow with a detailed test plan and updated TCO spreadsheet.

Per-1M tokens (ballpark, effective cost after platform efficiency):
- Redwood (hosted, standard quantized model, with batching and 60% cache hit): $85–$110 per 1M tokens.
- AWS Bedrock (managed, similar open model): ~$140–$180 per 1M tokens (billing tends to be higher for small/medium bursts; cold-starts and smaller batch sizes increase unit cost).
- OpenAI (api hosted models): ~$120–$160 per 1M tokens depending on model family.

Notes / assumptions:  
- Those ranges assume average request size ~1.2k tokens and continuous batching windows that achieve 8–12 tokens/request effective batching across GPUs.  
- With higher batching (e.g., sustained traffic producing 20–30 tokens/request average in the batch window) Redwood unit cost can go lower (~$60–$80 per 1M).
- Cache hit impact: at 60% KV/prefix cache hit we see ~35–45% reduction in token compute and that maps roughly linearly to token spend (so the Redwood $85–110 estimate already accounts for ~60% cache hit).
- Dedicated pricing for reserved capacity will be an order-match: fixed monthly commitment + lower unit pricing during committed hours; we can size reserved pools to cover 90–95% of expected peak traffic and use burst capacity for infrequent spikes.

Latency / throughput comments:  
- For the p95 < 120ms target with ~1.2k token requests, we recommend a Dedicated pool pinned to a family of GPU instances we previously validated for similar models.  
- If you require strict p95 under peak spikes, reserved headroom is recommended rather than pure autoscale. Autoscaling covers sustained increases but has a scaling latency.

Next tests we propose (Aditya will detail):
- Baseline: 1k concurrent workers, steady ramp to 5k rps to characterize p50/p95/p99 and any queuing.
- Batching analysis: vary client-side batching windows to see effective tokens/request and per-token cost curve.
- Cache simulation: inject synthetic prefix reuse to model 20/40/60/80% cache hit scenarios.
- Failover: validate fallback from Dedicated -> Hosted with circuit-breaker to ensure graceful degradation.

I attached the one-pager and TCO sheet; will update spreadsheet with the sample numbers once Aditya runs the first benchmark.

Marcus

Hi all — looping in the SE test plan and next steps.

Proposed test plan (week-of 2026-03-22 window):
1) Environment: run on Redwood Hosted first (to validate functional parity) then spin up a small Dedicated pool for the production-scale latency runs.
2) Benchmarks:
   - Throughput ramp: ramp to 5k rps over 30 minutes, hold for 10 minutes at peak to capture p50/p95/p99.
   - Batching sweep: test client batching windows [5ms, 10ms, 20ms, 50ms] and measure effective tokens/request and per-1M token unit cost.
   - Cache hit sweep: simulate 0/20/40/60/80% prefix reuse; measure token compute reduction and validate cache hit metric consistency.
   - Quantization matrix: run model at FP16 vs int8 quantized path to compare latency and quality delta (small eval set).
3) Metrics to collect: per-request tokens, compute tokens billed, effective unit cost per 1M tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and cache hit ratio.
4) Deliverables: updated TCO spreadsheet (attached) with measured numbers + a short recommendations doc for reserved pool sizing.

Logistics / asks from FastRetail:
- Provide a small representative prompt set (50–100 prompts) and an anonymized prefix reuse trace if possible.
- Confirm VPC/KMS constraints so we can include those in Dedicated sizing.
- Procurement: early signal on committed hours helps shape the reserved pricing proposal.

I’ve attached an initial TCO model populated with placeholder numbers (tco_modeling_1M_tokens.xlsx). I’ll run the first hosted benchmark Monday and share results by Tue EOD.

Thanks —
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
